newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt treasury bonds said set for September sale.
newsitem.headline: Egypt treasury bonds said set for September sale.

text.p: The Central Bank of Egypt will start taking applications for medium-term treasury bonds worth about four billion pounds during the first week of September, a government newspaper said on Tuesday.
A senior central bank official told Reuters that Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib had not yet approved the issue and nothing would be final until he did so.
The newspaper al-Masa quoted central bank governor Ismail Hassan as saying the interest rate on the bonds would be in line with prevailing rates in the market.
"It is expected that the interest rate will be 11 percent, one percent less than the interest on the first tranche," it added.
Hassan was quoted as saying the bank would accept applications up to the end of September and the bonds would be listed on the Egyptian stock exchange three months after issue.
The newspaper did not mention the maturity but Hassan has previously said that this will be between five and seven years.
A first tranche, issued in April 1995, was of five-year bonds worth three billion pounds. They pay a fixed 12 percent.
